narrative: During the 1950s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture were deeply rooted in tradition and identity. While specific details about hairstyles during this era are scarce, it can be inferred that cornrows, a style of three-strand braids close to the scalp, were likely worn by many. Cornrows are considered a traditional hairstyle of African braiding practice, as well as in the African diaspora, suggesting their presence in 1950s hair culture. The concept of protective hairstyles, which aim to reduce hair breakage and damage, may have also been employed during this time period. Unfortunately, documentation from this era is limited, and more research is needed to fully understand the nuances of Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture in the 1950s.
